# Erdős Problems via Bayesian Computation, I

40 Pages Posted: 3 Jul 2026

See all articles by Nicholas G. Polson

## Nicholas G. Polson

University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

## Vadim Sokolov

George Mason University

## Daniel Zantedeschi

University of South Florida - College of Business Administration

Date Written: June 10, 2026

### Abstract

We give Bayesian formulations of nine problems from the Erdős catalogue: Sidon and B h sets, distinct distances, intersecting families (Erdős-Ko-Rado), sunflower-free families, the critical Erdős-Rényi window, the longest increasing subsequence of a random permutation, the primitive-set conjecture, Bell inequalities on random graphs, and the Erdős discrepancy problem. For each problem we identify the deterministic question with a property of a posterior distribution under a natural prior, prove the main theorem, and quantify the remaining gap to the original conjecture. The toolkit emphasises sparse-recovery and structured priors: the horseshoe [Carvalho, Polson, and Scott, 2010], Polya-Inverse-Gamma augmentation [Polson, He, Xu, and Zhai, 2024], BART-style tree priors [Chipman, George, and McCulloch, 2010], Bayesian quadrature, particle learning, effective Kolmogorov complexity, and the exclusivity-graph framework for causal bounds. This toolkit is complementary to the Sanov / generative-Bayesiancomputation toolkit of the companion paper [Polson, Sokolov, and Zantedeschi, 2026]. Four numerical experiments illustrate the framework: horseshoe vs. LASSO Sidon recovery, Tracy-Widom convergence for the longest increasing subsequence, Bell violations on structured versus random graphs, and the critical-window distribution of the largest component.

Keywords: Bayesian Inference, Horseshoe Prior, Particle Learning, Sidon Sets, Intersecting Families, Sunflower-Free Sets, Tracy–Widom Distribution, Bell Inequalities, Erd˝os Discrepancy, Generative Bayesian Computation

# Transversal Six, Finite Obstructions and Boundary Profiles in Rank-Four Sunflower-Free Families

Version 13 · Final local edition · Evidence cutoff: 22 September 2026, America/New_York

Scope and review. This report distinguishes checked structural results, conditional implications and unresolved mathematical inputs. ## Abstract

We continue a Lean development for finite families of distinct four-element sets containing no sunflower with three distinct members, including sunflowers with empty core. Two retained version-twelve structural advances concern the actual original family. First, if every closed meeting neighborhood has at least fifty-four members, degree seventeen is impossible; every supported point consequently has degree at least eighteen. The proof combines an exact local trace inequality with the separated eight/nine decomposition of a degree-seventeen link, forcing the impossible incidence equation 5k=9. Under the still-explicit universal intersecting upper bound I(27), a hypothetical eighty-one-member family therefore has seventeen supported points and one of only two degree profiles: sixteen points of degree nineteen and one of degree twenty, or one point of degree eighteen, fourteen of degree nineteen and two of degree twenty. Second, an unconditional argument bounds the total number of degree-twenty points by two, with no family-size, support-size or I(27) assumption. Version thirteen proves that every nineteen-member sunflower-free triple family with maximum point degree at most five has transversal number exactly six. It also formalizes a universe-independent equivalence between I(27) and absence of a twenty-eight-member obstruction on eighty-five points, using an existing support argument, and exposes a direct two-profile census and three separate remaining proof obligations. These version-thirteen results extend the retained development. A primary-source recheck corrects the previous report's description of the author repository: substantial Lean sources exist, but the inspected rank-four declarations prove lower-bound witnesses rather than the universal intersecting upper bound.

### 6. A nineteen-link of maximum degree at most five has transversal number six

Theorem T6. Let L be a nineteen-member family of triples, with no three-petal sunflower, and suppose every point has degree at most five. Then L=A∪B with |A|=10, |B|=9, both components intersecting and their supports disjoint. Every transversal C of L satisfies |C|≥6, and there exists a transversal C⊆supp(L) with |C|=6. Consequently τ(L)=6.

The decomposition is inherited; the lower and upper transversal conclusions are checked version-thirteen extensions. For an anchor R∈L define s_L(R)=|{S∈L: |S∩R|=1}|, the total singleton-intersection count. This differs from the earlier point-indexed singleton trace. The inherited `singleton_intersection_card_le_nine` bounds it by nine. The meeting-incidence defect, including the anchor itself in the closed neighborhood, gives

$$2|M_L(R)|+1\le\sum_{x\in R}d_L(x)+s_L(R)\le15+9=24. \qquad\text{(E4)}$$

Integer rounding yields |M_L(R)|≤11, so the disjointness graph has minimum degree at least eight. 
The maximum-degree premise can equivalently be restricted to supported points: an unsupported point has degree zero. The checked interface `max_degree_iff_on_support` makes that equivalence explicit.

Corollary T6a. Any sunflower-free nineteen-triple family with a transversal of size at most five has a point of degree six. Indeed the universal triple-degree cap is six; absence of a degree-six point would force maximum degree five and contradict T6. The conclusion is stronger than the version-twelve threshold of four.

Corollary T6b. In an intersecting rank-four sunflower-free family with at least twenty members, a point x of degree nineteen has a distinct partner y of codegree six. A member avoiding x exists and is a four-point transversal of its link. Intersectingness is essential here; this corollary cannot be transferred silently to either unrestricted boundary profile.

Proposition T6c (the twenty-member endpoint is necessary). There is a nineteen-member intersecting rank-four sunflower-free family with a point of degree nineteen but no distinct point of codegree six with that center. Delete the block {0,1,2} from the inherited twenty-triple witness and adjoin one fresh common point to each remaining triple. Deletion preserves sunflower-freeness and the degree-at-most-five bound. Adjoining the common point preserves distinctness and turns any hypothetical sunflower into one in the original triple family after deletion. The new point lies in all nineteen members, while its codegree with every other point is at most five. The concrete construction over Option (Fin 12) is checked by `nineteen_member_endpoint_counterexample`. Thus weakening “at least twenty” in T6b to “at least nineteen” is mathematically false.

Proposition T6d (partner degree and exact pair-link geometry). In a twenty-eight-member intersecting rank-four sunflower-free family, a point of degree nineteen has a distinct codegree-six partner y with 6≤d(y)≤15. Inclusion-exclusion of the two original stars gives |star(x)∪star(y)|+6=19+d(y); the union lies in F, so d(y)+13≤28. The lower bound follows because the pair star is contained in the star at y. Both identities are checked on actual family filters.

More generally, every distinct pair of codegree six in a rank-four sunflower-free family has an exact residual link consisting of the three edges of one triangle and the three edges of a disjoint second triangle. All six residual points lie outside the pair. Restoring the pair to each residual edge recovers precisely the six original members in its star. The declaration `pair_codegree_six_exact_two_triangles` preserves all distinctness and disjointness conditions. It does not imply the existence of a global family satisfying an arbitrary collection of such local models.

On set-like sunflower-free families of subspaces over finite fields

The Erdős--Rado sunflower problem admits two natural analogues in finite vector spaces, corresponding to two different ways of generalising the set-theoretic notion of a sunflower. The first, used by Ihringer and Kupavskii [FFA 110 (2026) 102746], requires the petals to be in general position over the kernel; the second, used in the subspace codes literature (cf.\ Etzion--Raviv [DAM 186 (2015) 87-97], Blokhuis--De Boeck--D'haeseleer [DCC 90 (2022) 2101-2111]), requires only that the kernel equals the pairwise intersection of distinct petals. We refer to the second version as a \emph{set-like sunflower}, following Blokhuis, De Boeck and D'haeseleer. In this note, we focus on the set-like setting. {We first observe by illustrations that general-position sunflower-freeness does not imply set-like sunflower-freeness.} We then present a construction of set-like $s$-sunflower-free families of $k$-spaces \revised{in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ for $\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil \leq k \leq n-1$, of size $q^{n-k}$ (and $q^{n-k}+1$ for even $q$),} based on a manipulated version of the lifting construction; to our knowledge, this is the first systematic construction tailored to this setting. Finally, we compare the size of the construction with the exact optimum for small parameters, computed by exhaustive search.
